description:
Keeper Commander is a python-based CLI and SDK interface to the Keeper Security platform. Provides administrative controls, reporting, import/export and vault management.

Keeper Commander is a command-line and SDK interface to Keeper® Password Manager. Commander can be used to access and control your Keeper vault, perform administrative functions (such as end-user onboarding and data import/export), launch remote sessions, rotate passwords, eliminate hardcoded passwords and more. Keeper Commander is an open source project with contributions from Keeper's engineering team and partners.
Security
- Closes a Nested Share Folder (NSF) ownership bypass and attacker-shared folder name collisions. An attacker could share a folder with a victim using the same name as one of the victim's own folders (or a component of its path); Commander resolved the path to the first match, so `mkdir`, `mv`, `ln` and `record-add --folder` could route the victim's new folders, records and their keys into a folder the attacker owns, exposing them to the attacker. Path resolution now prefers owned folders, rejects ambiguous matches (including Secrets Manager application lookups) instead of picking the first one, and `record-add --folder` no longer creates an unfiled record when the folder cannot be resolved.
Features
- Delinea Secret Server migration, phase one: interactive Safe selection, a `--add-thycotic-users` option that creates the Delinea users in Keeper (with a dry-run preview), support for restricted secrets, and secret-level permissions.
- Adds an `--include-empty-folders` option to `import` and `export` so folders that contain no records are carried over (classic folders and NSF; export to JSON, CSV or KeePass).
- Adds PAM project support and filtering for shared folders in the membership commands.
Improvements
- `export` now requests attachment download links in batches of 100 instead of one request per attachment, which speeds up exports with many files; it falls back to per-file requests if a batch fails.
Fixes
- Service mode now returns the correct status when a PAM project extend succeeds.
- `pam action rotate` now uses the PAM Configuration named in the user's rotation settings. Previously a user linked to several configurations could be matched to the wrong one and fail with "Resource UID not found for record".
- An SSO user who chooses "SSO User with a Master Password" on a new device is no longer sent back to the SSO login page after device approval.
- The enterprise loader is reset when logging in.
- Tunnel resources no longer have their `meta` data replaced by `jit_settings` or `ai_settings`; the `meta` edge is now read by path.
- Usage text for sub-commands of command groups shows the full command name (for example `pam project import`) instead of only the group name.
- Invalid arguments to `ksm` no longer raise an extra error (the `ksm` subprocess exit code 2 is no longer re-raised).
Full commit range: `v18.1.9..v18.1.10`
